To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the currently fixated and the next word to the right are processed during the eye fixation and that this processing is necessary for fluent reading.
when word n+ 1 either disappeared or masked, there was considerable disruption of fluent reading.

the currently fixated (word n) word and/or the word (word n+ 1) to the right of the fixation are either disappearing or masked, there was disruption to reading, and there were robust frequency effect on the fixation of the fixated word.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the rightmost word on the line of text that is currently being processed in the fovea.
the cognitive and perceptual processes underlying reading and how these processes can be investigated with eye movement recording techniques.
the role of the word to right of fixation in reading.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
word n+1 is the word that is most critical to the eye movements when reading.
the word to the left of fixation is processed during the fixation on that word and the word to the immediate right of fixation is preprocessed before the fixation on that target word.
the word to the left of fixation is processed in a serial fashion, whereas the word to the immediate right of fixation is processed simultaneously with word n.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the word to the left of fixation is the primary determinant of fixation duration, but the word to the righth of fixation is the critical predictor of saccadic length.
readers need to process the upcoming word (word n+ 1) in order to read fluently.

the word to the left of fixation is important for the control of eye movements and for the processing of the word currently fixated, whereas the word to the immediate right of fixation is important to the control of the next eye movement and to the processing of the currently fixated words.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is the word to the left of fixation that is the primary source of cognitive/lingistic information for the current fixation.
the cognitive/linguistics processing that is required for fluent reading is robust to the loss of information from word n, but not word n+1.

it is important to have a clear understanding of the cognitive processes involved in the reading of text and how those processes influence reading behavior, especially when designing experiments to investigate eye movements when reading text.
